words.tr: adj. 脱离正道的；脱离常轨的
words.ex: His aberrant behavior surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他反常的行为让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An aberrant person or thing is one that is unusual or unexpected, especially in an unwelcome way.

words.tr: n. 脱离常规；误差；偏差；失常
words.ex: The sudden rain was an aberration in the dry season.
words.ex_cn: 这场突如其来的雨是旱季中的异常现象。
words.en: An aberration is an instance of straying from the normal or usual way, or something that is unusual or unexpected.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.tr:
adv. 光明正大地
adj. 光明正大的
words.ex: He always plays aboveboard in business.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业中总是光明正大。
words.en: If something is aboveboard, it is done in an honest and open way without any attempt to deceive.

words.tr: v. 废除；撤销
words.ex: The king abrogated the old law.
words.ex_cn: 国王废除了旧法律。
words.en: If someone in a position of authority abrogates something such as a law, agreement, or practice, they put an end to it.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.tr: adj. 难解的；深奥的
words.ex: The abstruse math problem confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个深奥的数学问题让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Difficult to understand; obscure.

words.tr: adj. 深不可测的；极坏的；糟透的
words.ex: The abysmal depth of the ocean scared the divers.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的深不可测吓到了潜水员。
words.en: If you describe a situation or the condition of something as abysmal, you think that it is very bad or poor in quality.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.tr: n. 赞扬；荣誉
words.ex: He received an accolade for his excellent work.
words.ex_cn: 他因出色的工作而获得了一项荣誉。
words.en: An accolade is something done or given to someone as a special honor or as a sign of approval.

words.tr: adj. 酸的； 苦涩的；尖刻的
words.ex: The lemon juice had an acerbic taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁有酸味。
words.en: If you say something acerbic, or harshly bitter, you are being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.tr: n. 顶点；极点；巅峰；
words.ex: The acme of his career was winning the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的顶点是获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: The highest point of achievement or excellence.

words.tr: n. 尖刻的言辞；激烈的争吵
words.ex: There was acrimony between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间充满了敌意。
words.en: Bitterness or ill feeling.

words.tr: adj. 坚定不移的；
words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.tr: adj. 足够的；
words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.tr: v. 判决；裁定
words.ex: The judge will adjudicate the dispute next week.
words.ex_cn: 法官将在下周裁决这场纠纷。
words.en: To adjudicate means to make an official decision about a problem or dispute.

words.tr: v. 劝告；警告；训诫
words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 劝告的，警告的
words.ex: The teacher's tone was admonitory, warning us to be careful.
words.ex_cn: 老师的语气是劝告的，警告我们要小心。
words.en: Serving to warn or advise, especially in a gentle or earnest manner.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.tr: n. 审美家；唯美主义者
words.ex: He is an aesthete who loves beautiful art.
words.ex_cn: 他是个热爱美好艺术的唯美主义者。
words.en: An aesthete is someone who has a deep appreciation for beauty and art, often to the point of being considered a connoisseur.

words.tr: adj. 审美的；美学的；
words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.tr: adj. 谦恭有礼的；和蔼可亲的
words.ex: He is an affable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is affable is pleasant and friendly.

words.tr: adj. 富裕的；富足的；
words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.tr: n. 敏捷；活泼；欣然；乐意
words.ex: He answered the question with alacrity.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地回答了问题。
words.en: If you do something with alacrity, you do it quickly and eagerly.

words.tr: n. 利他主义；利他；
words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.tr: n. 汞合金；混合物
words.ex: The dentist used an amalgam to fill the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医用汞合金填补了蛀牙。
words.en: An amalgam is a mixture of mercury and another metal, especially one used by dentists to fill holes in teeth. It can also refer to a mixture of different things.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: adj. 矛盾的；
words.ex: He felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他对接受这份工作邀约感到矛盾。
words.en: If you say that someone is ambivalent about something, you mean that they have mixed feelings about it or are unsure whether they want it or not.

words.tr: v. 改善；
words.ex: The new policy will ameliorate living conditions.
words.ex_cn: 新政策将改善生活条件。
words.en: To make something better or improve a situation.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的
words.ex: He is amenable to new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意接受新想法。
words.en: If you are amenable to something, you are willing to do it or accept it.

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.tr:
adv. 狂暴地；狂怒地；杀气腾腾地
adj. 狂暴的；狂怒的；杀气腾腾的
words.ex: The dog ran amok in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 狗在花园里乱跑。
words.en: If someone runs amok, they behave in a wild and uncontrolled manner, often causing damage or harm.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.tr: adv. 充足地；
words.ex: The food was amply provided for all guests.
words.ex_cn: 所有客人的食物都充足地提供了。
words.en: If something is amply demonstrated, proved, or rewarded, it is shown, proven, or rewarded in a very obvious and satisfactory way.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.tr: adj. 相似的；类似的；
words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.tr: n. 诅咒；受诅咒的事；逐出教门；十分讨厌的人（或事物）
words.ex: Lying is anathema to her.
words.ex_cn: 说谎是她所诅咒的。
words.en: Something or someone that one vehemently dislikes.

words.tr: adj. 贫血的；患贫血症的；衰弱无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He looks anemic after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病很久后看起来很苍白。
words.en: If someone is anemic, they are suffering from anemia, which means they have a lower than normal number of red blood cells or hemoglobin, making them feel tired and weak.

words.tr: n. 仇恨；憎恶；敌意
words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.tr:
adj. 乏味无趣的；四平八稳的；不得罪人的；止痛的
n. 止痛药
words.ex: The meeting was anodyne and made everyone sleepy.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议乏味无趣，让所有人都犯困。
words.en: An anodyne is something that soothes, comforts, or relieves pain.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr: n. 异常事物；反常现象；
words.ex: The strange weather this month is an anomaly.
words.ex_cn: 这个月奇怪的天气是一个异常现象。
words.en: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.tr: v. 先于；提早日期
words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；古怪的
words.ex: His antic behavior made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他滑稽的行为让大家都笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antic, you mean that it is strange and foolish in a way that is amusing.

words.tr: n. 反感；
words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；
words.ex: The old computer is antiquated and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧电脑过时且缓慢。
words.en: Something that is antiquated is old-fashioned or outdated and no longer suitable for modern conditions or purposes.

words.tr: adj. 对偶的；对立的
words.ex: His views are antithetical to hers.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与她的观点是对偶的。
words.en: Directly opposed or contrasted; mutually incompatible.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏兴趣的；漠不关心的；
words.ex: He was apathetic about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影缺乏兴趣。
words.en: If you describe someone as apathetic, you are criticizing them because they do not seem to be interested in or enthusiastic about doing anything.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；
words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.tr: n. 最高点；顶点；
words.ex: The apex of the mountain is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 山的最高点被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or top of something; the climax or culmination of something.

words.tr: n. 格言；警句
words.ex: He told an aphorism about patience.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一句关于耐心的格言。
words.en: An aphorism is a short, clever saying that expresses a general truth or observation.

words.tr: adj. 警句（似）的；格言（似）的
words.ex: His writing is often aphoristic, full of concise wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 他的写作常常充满格言般的简洁智慧。
words.en: Relating to or resembling an aphorism; concise and containing a general truth.

words.tr: n. 沉着；镇定
words.ex: She spoke with aplomb during the interview.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试中自信地发言。
words.en: If you do something with aplomb, you do it with confidence in a relaxed way.

words.tr: adj. 真实性可疑的；杜撰的
words.ex: The story about the ghost is apocryphal.
words.ex_cn: 关于鬼魂的故事是不可信的。
words.en: An apocryphal story is one that is probably not true or did not happen, although it is often told and believed by some people to be true.

words.tr: n. 顶峰；顶点；最高点
words.ex: The moon reached its apogee last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚月亮到达了远地点。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; a climax or culmination.

words.tr: n. 叛教者；脱党者；变节者
words.ex: He became an apostate after leaving the church.
words.ex_cn: 他离开教会后成了叛教者。
words.en: An apostate is someone who has abandoned their religious faith, political loyalties, or principles.

words.tr: n. 格言；箴言
words.ex: The teacher often quoted an apothegm to emphasize a point.
words.ex_cn: 老师经常引用一句格言来强调一个观点。
words.en: An apothegm is a short, pithy, and instructive saying or formulation; a maxim.

words.tr: n. 鼎盛时期；（人生或事业的)巅峰；册封为神
words.ex: The artist's work reached apotheosis in his final masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品在他的最终杰作中达到了神化。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; culmination or climax.

words.tr: v. 缓和；平息；使满足
words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.tr: adj. 可觉察的；很可观的
words.ex: There is an appreciable difference in his grades.
words.ex_cn: 他的成绩有明显的差异。
words.en: If something is appreciable, it is large enough to be noticed or considered important.

words.tr: n. 担忧；恐惧；逮捕
words.ex: He felt apprehension before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到焦虑。
words.en: Anxiety or fear that something bad or unpleasant will happen; understanding; the action of arresting someone.

words.tr: adj. 认可的；赞赏的
words.ex: His performance received approbatory remarks from the critics.
words.ex_cn: 他的表演受到了评论家们的赞赏性评价。
words.en: Expressing approval or commendation.

words.tr: adj. 适当的；合适的；恰当的；
words.ex: This dress is appropriate for a wedding.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子适合参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is appropriate is suitable or acceptable for a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 附属的，从属的; n. 附属物（等于 appurtenance）
words.ex: The appurtenant structures include the garage and the shed.
words.ex_cn: 附属结构包括车库和棚屋。
words.en: Belonging or related to something as an adjunct or accessory.

words.tr: adj. 任意的；
words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.tr: adj. 晦涩难解的；
words.ex: The ancient text contained arcane symbols that no one could understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本古籍中包含着无人能理解的晦涩难解的符号。
words.en: Arcane refers to something that is mysterious or difficult to understand, often because it is known or understood by only a few people.

words.tr: n. 拱形；拱门；弧形；
words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

words.tr: adj. 古老的；过时的
words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 艰巨的；费力的；
words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr: adj. 坏透的；彻头彻尾的
words.ex: He is an arrant fool for saying that.
words.ex_cn: 他说那样的话，真是个十足的傻瓜。
words.en: You use arrant to emphasize that someone or something is completely bad or has a bad quality.

words.tr: n. 暴发户；一心想发迹的人；野心家
words.ex: The arriviste tried to buy his way into high society.
words.ex_cn: 那个暴发户试图用金钱打入上流社会。
words.en: An arriviste is someone who is eager to gain wealth or power and is often considered to lack the social graces or sophistication of someone who has been wealthy or powerful for a long time.

words.tr: v. 非法霸占；僭越；盗用
words.ex: He arrogated the right to make decisions without consulting the team.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自决定，未经团队商议。
words.en: To claim or seize without justification; to assume or appropriate to oneself without right.

words.tr: adj. 巧妙的；有技巧的；
words.ex: He gave an artful answer to the tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个棘手的问题给出了一个巧妙的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as artful, you mean that they are clever and skillful at achieving what they want, especially by deceiving people.

words.tr: n. 诡计；
words.ex: He used artifice to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计赢得了比赛。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；自然的；不做作的
words.ex: Her artless smile made everyone feel at ease.
words.ex_cn: 她那天真的微笑让每个人都感到轻松。
words.en: If you describe someone as artless, you mean that they are simple and honest, and do not try to deceive other people.

words.tr: n. 优势；支配地位；支配力量
words.ex: The king's ascendancy lasted for twenty years.
words.ex_cn: 国王的统治持续了二十年。
words.en: If one group has ascendancy over another group, it has more power or influence than the other group.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.tr: v. 把…归因于
words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.tr: adv. 斜视地；怀疑地；不赞许地
words.ex: He looked askance at the strange offer.
words.ex_cn: 他斜眼看着这个奇怪的提议。
words.en: If you look askance at something, you look at it in a way that shows you are suspicious or do not approve of it.

words.tr: n. 严酷；粗暴；刻薄
words.ex: The asperity of the terrain made the hike difficult.
words.ex_cn: 地形的粗糙使得徒步旅行变得困难。
words.en: If you say something with asperity, you say it in a harsh, severe way.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.tr: v. 缓和；减轻
words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.tr: n. 返祖现象；
words.ex: His fear of the dark is an atavism from our ancestors.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗的恐惧是我们祖先的返祖现象。
words.en: The reappearance in an organism of characteristics of some remote ancestor that have been absent in intervening generations.

words.tr: v. 使减细；使减小；使减弱
words.ex: The wire attenuates as it gets longer.
words.ex_cn: 这根电线随着变长而变细。
words.en: To reduce the force, effect, or value of something.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.tr: n. 大胆；鲁莽；厚颜
words.ex: He had the audacity to lie to his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老板撒谎。
words.en: Audacity is the willingness to take bold risks, often in a way that shocks or surprises people.

words.tr: v. 增强；
words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.tr: adj. 吉利的；有利的
words.ex: It was an auspicious day for their wedding.
words.ex_cn: 那天是他们婚礼的吉日。
words.en: If you describe something as auspicious, you mean that it is a sign of future success.

words.tr: adj. 简朴的；严厉的；苦行的；紧缩的
words.ex: The room has austere walls with no decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的墙壁朴素，没有任何装饰。
words.en: If you describe something as austere, you approve of its plain and simple appearance.

words.tr: adj. 独裁的；专制的；
words.ex: The autocratic leader made all decisions without asking others.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁的领导人独自做出所有决定，从不询问他人。
words.en: If you describe someone as autocratic, you are criticizing them because they have complete power and make decisions without asking anyone else's advice.

words.tr: n. 贪婪；贪财
words.ex: His avarice knew no bounds, always seeking more wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪无止境，总是追求更多的财富。
words.en: Avarice is extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.tr: adj. 贪财的；贪婪的
words.ex: He is avaricious and always wants more money.
words.ex_cn: 他贪婪，总是想要更多的钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as avaricious, you are criticizing them because they have an extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.tr: v. 避免；防止；
words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.tr: adj. 热衷的；
words.ex: He is an avid reader of mystery novels.
words.ex_cn: 他热衷于阅读侦探小说。
words.en: If you say that someone is avid for something, you mean that they are very eager to get it.

words.tr: n. 獾皮毛；
words.ex: He wore a coat made of badger.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件用獾皮毛制成的外套。
words.en: To badger someone means to repeatedly ask them to do something or to repeatedly question them about something, often in an annoying way.

words.tr: adj. 凶恶的；恶意的
words.ex: The baleful glare of the enemy sent shivers down their spines.
words.ex_cn: 敌人恶意的目光让他们不寒而栗。
words.en: Baleful means threatening harm or evil.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；刻苦的
words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.tr: adj. 平庸的；
words.ex: The movie had a banal plot that everyone had seen before.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的剧情平庸得让人看过了无数次。
words.en: If you describe something as banal, you do not like it because you think that it is so ordinary that it is not at all effective or interesting.

words.tr: n. 平凡；琐事
words.ex: The movie was full of banality and had no original ideas.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影充满了陈词滥调，没有任何新意。
words.en: The quality of being banal; unoriginality.

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.tr: v. 掩饰；
words.ex: His smile belieed his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑掩饰了他真实的情感。
words.en: If one thing belies another, it hides the true situation and so creates a false idea or image of someone or something.

words.tr: v. 轻视；贬低；小看
words.ex: He tries to belittle his brother's success.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低他哥哥的成功。
words.en: To belittle someone or something means to make them seem less important or less good than they really are.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的
words.ex: He is bellicose when he drinks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他喝多了时就好战。
words.en: Having or showing a tendency to argue or fight.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.tr: v. 悲悼；哀叹
words.ex: He bemoans the loss of his old car.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨失去了他的旧车。
words.en: If you bemoan something, you express sorrow or dissatisfaction about it.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧无知的；落后的；未开发的
words.ex: The village remained benighted and untouched by modern civilization.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄仍然愚昧无知，未受现代文明的影响。
words.en: If you describe people or the place where they live as benighted, you think they are unfortunate or do not know anything.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；
words.ex: The benign teacher always helped students after class.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师总是在课后帮助学生。
words.en: A benign substance or process does not have any harmful effects.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was bereft of words after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他一句话也说不出来。
words.en: If someone is bereft of something, they have lost it and feel its loss keenly.

words.tr: v. 围困；围攻
words.ex: The army besiege the small town.
words.ex_cn: 军队围攻这座小镇。
words.en: To surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender; to overwhelm someone with requests or complaints.

words.tr: v. 诋毁；玷污
words.ex: His reputation was besmirched by the false accusations.
words.ex_cn: 他的名声被这些虚假的指控玷污了。
words.en: To besmirch someone or something means to spoil their good reputation.

words.tr: adj. 迷恋的；爱得发狂的
words.ex: He was completely besotted with her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她爱得发狂。
words.en: If you are besotted with someone or something, you are so infatuated with them that you behave in a foolish or irrational way.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.tr: adj. 胆汁的；患胆病的；脾气暴躁的；恶心头痛的；让人恶心的
words.ex: He had a bilious complexion due to his illness.
words.ex_cn: 由于生病，他的脸色发黄。
words.en: If someone is bilious, they are bad-tempered or irritable, often because of a problem with their liver or digestion.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；公然的；喧闹的
words.ex: He made a blatant lie to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他为了逃避惩罚，公然撒了谎。
words.en: If you describe an action as blatant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way, often with a lack of shame or embarrassment.

words.tr: adj. 无望的；凄凉的；荒凉的；
words.ex: The future looks bleak without a job.
words.ex_cn: 没有工作，未来看起来毫无希望。
words.en: If you describe a situation as bleak, you mean that it seems unlikely to improve or get better.

words.tr: v. 增强；提高；
words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: n. 裨益；
words.ex: Clean water is a boon to the village.
words.ex_cn: 干净的水对这个村庄是有益的。
words.en: A boon is something that is very helpful and improves the quality of life.

words.tr: adj. 乡巴佬的；粗野的；粗鄙的
words.ex: His boorish behavior made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他粗俗的行为让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as boorish, you mean their behavior is unrefined, insensitive, or rude.

words.tr: v. 删节猥亵不当的部分
words.ex: The publisher decided to bowdlerize the novel to make it suitable for younger readers.
words.ex_cn: 出版商决定删改这本小说，使其适合年轻读者阅读。
words.en: To bowdlerize a book or film means to remove parts of it that are considered offensive or improper, especially in order to make it suitable for children or for people who might be offended.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.tr:
n. 马笼头；缰绳；约束
v. 套笼头；表示恼怒；抑制
words.ex: He pulled the bridle to stop the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他拉了一下缰绳让马停下来。
words.en: A bridle is a set of straps that fits around a horse's head and is used to control the horse. As a verb, to bridle means to put a bridle on a horse or to restrain or control something.

words.tr:
n. 刚毛；猪鬃
v. 大为恼怒；耸起毛发
words.ex: The brush has stiff bristles for cleaning pots.
words.ex_cn: 这把刷子有坚硬的刚毛，用来清洗锅具。
words.en: A bristle is a short, stiff hair, usually one of many on an animal or brush. As a verb, it can mean to react angrily or defensively, or (of hair or fur) to stand upright away from the skin, typically as a sign of anger or fear.

words.tr:
n. 舷侧；舷炮齐射；猛烈攻击
adv. 一侧对着某物
words.ex: The ship fired a broadside at the enemy vessel.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船向敌舰舷侧开火。
words.en: A broadside is the side of a ship; the simultaneous discharge of guns on one side of a ship; or a strongly worded critical attack.

words.tr: n. 溴化物；溴化物镇静剂；陈腔滥调
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a bromide for his anxiety.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种溴化物来治疗焦虑。
words.en: A bromide is a chemical compound containing bromine, or a remark or statement that is unoriginal and used too often.

words.tr:
n. 小河；溪
v. （不）忍受；（不）容忍
words.ex: The child jumps over the brook.
words.ex_cn: 孩子跳过小溪。
words.en: A small stream; to tolerate or allow something.

words.tr: v. 威吓；威逼；恫吓
words.ex: She tried to browbeat him into submission.
words.ex_cn: 她试图恫吓他屈服。
words.en: To intimidate or bully someone into doing something, especially by using threats or aggressive behavior.

words.tr:
n. 雄鹿；公羊；雄兔；美元
v. （马等）猛然弓背跃起；抵制
words.ex: The buck ran through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 雄鹿在森林中奔跑。
words.en: A buck is a male deer, antelope, rabbit, or hare. It can also refer to a dollar in American slang. As a verb, it means to jump or to resist something.

words.tr: adj. 乡村的；田园的
words.ex: He loves the bucolic life in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢乡村的田园生活。
words.en: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.

words.tr: adj. 装模作样的；笨手笨脚的；爱管闲事的；胡乱的; v. 笨手笨脚；跌跌撞撞地前进；模糊不清地说...
words.ex: His bumbling smile made everyone feel he was pretending to be friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他装模作样的微笑让所有人都觉得他是在假装友好。
words.en: If you describe someone as bumbling, you mean that they behave in a confused, disorganized way, making mistakes and usually not achieving anything.

words.tr: v. 迅速生长；急速增长
words.ex: The flowers burgeon in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，花朵绽放。
words.en: To grow or develop quickly; to flourish.

words.tr:
n. 扶墙；拱壁
v. 支持
words.ex: The old wall needs a buttress to stay standing.
words.ex_cn: 这面旧墙需要一个支撑物来保持不倒。
words.en: A buttress is a structure built against or projecting from a wall which serves to support or reinforce the wall. As a verb, to buttress means to support or strengthen something.

words.tr: adj. 拜占庭风格的；
words.ex: The church has a byzantine dome with gold mosaics.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂有一个拜占庭风格的穹顶，饰有金色马赛克。
words.en: If you describe a system or process as byzantine, you are criticizing it because it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；像尸体的；枯槁的
words.ex: His cadaverous appearance frightened the children.
words.ex_cn: 他那尸体般的惨白面容吓坏了孩子们。
words.en: If you describe someone as cadaverous, you mean they are extremely thin and pale.

words.tr: adj. 未成熟的；无处世经验的；乳臭未干的
words.ex: The new recruits were callow and inexperienced.
words.ex_cn: 新兵们年轻而无经验。
words.en: If you describe someone as callow, you mean that they are inexperienced and immature.

words.tr: n. 诬蔑；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.tr: n. 谣传；误传
words.ex: The story was a complete canard, spread by those with vested interests.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事完全是一个谣言，是由那些有既得利益的人散布的。
words.en: A canard is a false or baseless story or piece of information, especially one that is deliberately misleading.

words.tr: adj. 坦率的；坦诚的；偷拍的
words.ex: He gave a candid answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了坦率的回答。
words.en: If you are candid, you are honest and say what you really think.

words.tr: n. 能力；容量；身份；
words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr: v. （有条件）投降；屈从
words.ex: The army will not capitulate to the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 军队不会向敌人投降。
words.en: If you capitulate, you stop resisting and do what someone else wants you to do.

words.tr: adj. 变化无常的；任性的
words.ex: He is capricious and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is capricious often changes their mind unexpectedly.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr:
adj. 吹毛求疵的；挑毛病的
v. 挑剔；吹毛求疵；发牢骚；“carp”的现在分词
words.ex: His constant carping criticism was tiresome.
words.ex_cn: 他那没完没了的吹毛求疵的批评令人厌烦。
words.en: If you describe someone as carping, you mean that they keep criticizing or complaining about someone or something, especially in a way you think is unnecessary or annoying.

words.tr: v. 严惩；鞭打；谴责
words.ex: The teacher castigated the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师因学生作弊而严厉批评了他。
words.en: To castigate someone means to criticize or punish them severely.

words.tr: n. 大灾难；洪水；剧变
words.ex: The earthquake was a sudden cataclysm.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场突如其来的灾难。
words.en: A cataclysm is an event that causes great damage or makes a big change to something.

words.tr: n. 催化剂；接触剂；
words.ex: The enzyme acts as a catalyst in the reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这种酶在反应中充当催化剂。
words.en: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a person or thing that precipitates a change.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.tr:
n. 骑士；勋章获得者；骑士风度的男子
adj. 傲慢的；豪强的；（对女人）献殷勤的；大方的
words.ex: The knight rode on a horse like a cavalier.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士骑着马，像个骑士一样。
words.en: If you describe someone as cavalier, you are criticizing them because you think that they do not consider other people's feelings or take account of the seriousness of a situation.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.tr: n. 迅速；敏捷
words.ex: The project was completed with remarkable celerity.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目以惊人的速度完成了。
words.en: Celerity is the quality of being swift or rapid.

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.tr: adj. 大脑的；理智的
words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.tr: n. 懊恼
words.ex: He felt chagrin when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛时感到懊恼。
words.en: Chagrin is a feeling of disappointment, upset, or annoyance, perhaps because of your own failure.

words.tr: n. 优胜者；冠军；
words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.tr: adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He is chary of spending money on useless things.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意把钱花在无用的东西上。
words.en: If you are chary of doing something, you are cautious or hesitant about doing it because you are worried that it might have bad consequences.

words.tr: v. 严惩；责难；鞭笞
words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.tr: n. 沙文主义；盲目的爱国心
words.ex: He shows chauvinism by thinking men are better than women.
words.ex_cn: 他认为男人比女人更好，表现出大男子主义。
words.en: Chauvinism is the strong and unreasonable belief that your own country or race is the best or most important.

words.tr:
adj. 沙文主义的；本着…第一主义者
n. 沙文主义者；盲目的爱国者
words.ex: He is a chauvinist who thinks men are better than women.
words.ex_cn: 他是个沙文主义者，认为男人比女人优秀。
words.en: A chauvinist is a person who believes in the superiority of their own group, especially their own gender or nationality, often to the point of being prejudiced against other groups.

words.tr:
v. 检查；核对；
n. 检查；支票；阻止；
words.ex: Please check your homework before class.
words.ex_cn: 请在上课前检查你的作业。
words.en: To examine something in order to determine its accuracy, quality, or condition, or to make sure that something is correct or safe.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr: n. 喀迈拉；妄想；嵌合体
words.ex: The myth says the chimera has a lion's head, a goat's body, and a snake's tail.
words.ex_cn: 这个神话说喀迈拉有狮子的头、山羊的身体和蛇的尾巴。
words.en: In Greek mythology, a chimera is a creature that is composed of parts of different animals. In modern usage, it refers to an illusion or fabrication of the mind; especially an unrealizable dream.

words.tr: adj. 有骑士风度的；彬彬有礼的；侠义的
words.ex: The knight was chivalrous and helped the lady.
words.ex_cn: 这位骑士有骑士精神，帮助了那位女士。
words.en: A chivalrous man is polite, kind, and unselfish, especially towards women.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；暴躁的；脾气不好的
words.ex: He is a choleric man who shouts when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个易怒的人，一生气就大喊大叫。
words.en: A choleric person is someone who gets angry very easily.

words.tr:
v. 高兴得咯咯笑；哈哈大笑
n. 哈哈大笑；开心地笑
words.ex: He chortled when he saw the funny cat.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的猫时咯咯笑了。
words.en: To laugh in a breathy, gleeful way; chuckle.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；无礼的；脾气坏的
words.ex: His churlish behavior at the meeting was uncalled for.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上的粗鲁行为是完全没有必要的。
words.en: If someone is churlish, they are rude, bad-tempered, and impolite.

words.tr: v. 限制；
words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.tr: v. 绕行；设法避开；智胜；围住
words.ex: He circumvented the traffic by taking a small road.
words.ex_cn: 他通过走一条小路绕过了交通拥堵。
words.en: If someone circumvents a rule or restriction, they avoid having to obey it, usually in a clever and dishonest way.

words.tr: n. 仁慈；宽厚；温和
words.ex: The judge showed clemency and reduced the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 法官表现出宽大，减轻了刑罚。
words.en: Clemency is kindness and forgiveness, especially towards someone who could be punished severely.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.tr: adj. 有凝聚性的；
words.ex: The team showed cohesive behavior during the project.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队在项目期间表现出有凝聚力的行为。
words.en: If something is cohesive, it consists of parts that fit together well and form a united whole.

words.tr: n. 共谋；勾结
words.ex: The two companies were accused of collusion to fix prices.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司被指控串通操纵价格。
words.en: Collusion is secret or illegal cooperation or conspiracy, especially in order to cheat or deceive others.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；庞大的；
words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 值得赞扬的；
words.ex: His commendable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞扬的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as commendable, you approve of it or are praising it.

words.tr: adj. 相称的；相当的
words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.tr: adj. 免费赠送的；
words.ex: The hotel gave us complimentary breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 酒店免费赠送了我们早餐。
words.en: If something is complimentary, it is given or done free of charge. It can also mean expressing a compliment; praising or approving.

words.tr: adj. 有同谋关系的，串通一气的
words.ex: She felt complicit in the scheme.
words.ex_cn: 她觉得自己也参与了这个阴谋。
words.en: If someone is complicit in a crime or wrongdoing, they are involved in it or associated with it, often without taking active part in the actual wrongdoing.

words.tr:
n. 化合物；
adj. 复合的；混合的；
words.ex: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
words.ex_cn: 水是由氢和氧组成的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr: v. 承认（失败）；
words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.tr: v. 安抚；讨好；使息怒；调和
words.ex: He tried to conciliate his angry neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图安抚他生气的邻居。
words.en: If you conciliate someone, you try to end a disagreement with them by doing or saying things that will make them less angry or more friendly.

words.tr: n. 同时发生的事；
words.ex: The rain was a concomitant of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨水是这场风暴的同时发生的事。
words.en: Something that is concomitant with something else, especially something undesirable, happens at the same time as it or is connected with it.

words.tr: adj. 有利于…的
words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.tr: n. 大火；大火灾
words.ex: The conflagration destroyed the whole forest.
words.ex_cn: 这场大火烧毁了整个森林。
words.en: A conflagration is a large and destructive fire that causes considerable damage.

words.tr: v. 理应；有必要
words.ex: It behooves us to be cautious in our decisions.
words.ex_cn: 我们在做决定时理应谨慎。
words.en: If it behooves you to do something, it is right, necessary, or useful for you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；莽撞的；唐突的
words.ex: He gave a brusque answer and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁地回答了一句，然后走开了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as brusque, you mean that they deal with or say things quickly and shortly, so that they seem to be rude.

words.tr: v. 合并；混合
words.ex: He conflates happiness with wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福和财富混为一谈。
words.en: To combine two or more things into one, especially in a way that is confusing or misleading.

words.tr: v. 使疑惑；
words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr: v. 纵容；默许；共谋
words.ex: The teacher connived at the students' cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师纵容了学生的作弊行为。
words.en: If one person connives with another to do something wrong, they secretly allow or help them to do it.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.tr: adj. 显眼的；显著的；
words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.tr: n. 限制；约束；
words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.tr:
v. 完成；使完美；圆房
adj. 完美的；至上的；圆满的
words.ex: He consummated the deal with a handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他用握手完成了这笔交易。
words.en: To consummate means to make something complete or perfect, often used in the context of a marriage or an agreement. It can also describe someone who is extremely skilled in a particular area.

words.tr: adj. 轻蔑的；瞧不起的
words.ex: He gave a contemptuous smile when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 当她说话时，他露出轻蔑的微笑。
words.en: If you are contemptuous of someone or something, you do not like or respect them at all.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 依情况而定的；
words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.tr: adj. 深感懊悔的；痛悔的；悔悟的
words.ex: He felt contrite after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt.

words.tr: n. 痛悔；悔罪；悔悟
words.ex: He felt contrition after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: The state of feeling remorseful and penitent.

words.tr: v. 设法做到；
words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.tr: n. 谜语；难题；
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.tr: adj. 欢乐的；轻松快活的；好交际的
words.ex: The party was convivial and everyone laughed a lot.
words.ex_cn: 派对气氛友好愉快，大家都笑得很开心。
words.en: A convivial atmosphere or event is friendly and pleasant, and people enjoy being together.

words.tr:
adj. 旋绕的；费解的
v. 盘旋；卷绕；“convolute”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The path through the garden was convoluted.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的小路蜿蜒曲折。
words.en: If you describe something such as a story, explanation, or system as convoluted, you mean that it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；丰富的
words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: n. 丰饶的山羊角；聚宝盆；丰饶角
words.ex: The Thanksgiving table had a cornucopia of fruits and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 感恩节的餐桌上摆满了水果和蔬菜的丰饶山羊角。
words.en: A cornucopia is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly represented as a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts.

words.tr: n. 必然的结果（或结论）；推论
words.ex: The theorem leads to a simple corollary.
words.ex_cn: 这个定理引出了一个简单的推论。
words.en: A corollary is a statement that follows on from another statement, and that is usually easily understood or proved.

words.tr: v. 证实；
words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.tr: adj. 有共同边界的； 毗连的
words.ex: The two regions are coterminous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个区域是边界相连的。
words.en: Having the same boundaries or limits; sharing a common border.

words.tr:
n. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
v. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: If you countermand an order, you cancel it, usually by giving a different order.

words.tr: n. 母牛；奶牛；
words.ex: The farmer milks the cow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给母牛挤奶。
words.en: A cow is a large female animal that is kept on farms for its milk.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.tr: n. 可信性；
words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.tr: adj. 值得赞扬的；道德的
words.ex: His performance was creditable despite the difficult circumstances.
words.ex_cn: 尽管处境艰难，他的表现仍然值得称赞。
words.en: Deserving praise or approval; trustworthy.

words.tr: n. 轻信；易信
words.ex: His credulity made him an easy target for scams.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻信使他很容易成为诈骗的目标。
words.en: Credulity is a willingness to believe that something is real or true, especially when this is based on insufficient evidence.

words.tr: adj. 垂头丧气的；灰心失望的
words.ex: He looked crestfallen after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后看起来垂头丧气。
words.en: If you are crestfallen, you are disappointed and sad because of something that has happened.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 结晶；定形；（使）具体化；变明确
words.ex: The idea began to crystallize after many talks.
words.ex_cn: 经过多次讨论，这个想法开始明朗起来。
words.en: To crystallize means to cause something to form into crystals or to become clear and definite in form.

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.tr: n. 有罪；可责
words.ex: The court found him not guilty, but acknowledged his culpability in the incident.
words.ex_cn: 法庭判他无罪，但承认他在事件中的过失。
words.en: The state of being responsible for a fault or wrong; blame.

words.tr: adj. 复杂而低效的；
words.ex: The old system is cumbersome and slow.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧系统复杂而低效。
words.en: Something that is cumbersome is large and heavy and therefore difficult to carry, wear, or handle.

words.tr: n. 贪心；贪婪
words.ex: His cupidity led him to make risky investments.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪导致他进行了高风险的投资。
words.en: Intense desire for wealth or possessions; greed.

words.tr: n. （年纪大的）坏脾气的人；脾气暴躁的人
words.ex: He was known as a curmudgeon who rarely smiled.
words.ex_cn: 他以脾气坏著称，很少笑。
words.en: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered or difficult person, especially an old one.

words.tr: n. 缺乏；
words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: v. 贬低；降格；贬损
words.ex: He tried to debase the coin with cheap metal.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用廉价金属贬低硬币的价值。
words.en: To debase something means to reduce its value or quality.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.tr: v. 揭穿真相；暴露
words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.tr: n. 大批杀害；
words.ex: The war led to the decimation of the village population.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争导致了该村人口的大批杀害。
words.en: The act of killing or destroying a large part of a group or population.

words.tr: adj. 符合礼仪的；得体的；高雅的
words.ex: She behaved in a decorous way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上举止得体。
words.en: If you say that something is decorous, you mean that it is dignified, proper, and socially acceptable.

words.tr: n. 礼貌得体；适宜的举止
words.ex: He maintained decorum during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持了得体的行为。
words.en: Decorum is behavior that is controlled, calm, and polite, especially in formal situations.

words.tr: v. 公开反对；谴责
words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.tr: adj. 恭敬的；顺从的
words.ex: He was deferential to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师很恭敬。
words.en: If you are deferential, you are polite and respectful towards someone, especially because they have a higher position or status than you.

words.tr: v. 支付
words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.tr: v. 退化；
words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.tr: v. 屈尊；施惠于人
words.ex: He did not deign to answer her question.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑于回答她的问题。
words.en: If someone deigns to do something, they do it unwillingly and with a feeling of superiority.

words.tr: v. 委派；
words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.tr: v. 描画；划定（边界）
words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: v. 贬低；降低
words.ex: He tries not to demean his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不贬低他的同学。
words.en: To demean someone or something means to cause them to lose their dignity or respect.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.tr: adj. 娴静的；端庄的；假装矜持的
words.ex: She is a demure girl who never speaks loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个文静的女孩，从不大声说话。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a young woman, as demure, you mean they are quiet, shy, and behave so that they do not attract attention to themselves.

words.tr: v. 诋毁；贬低；诬蔑
words.ex: He tries to denigrate his rival's ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他试图贬低对手的想法。
words.en: If you denigrate someone or something, you criticize them unfairly or insult them.

words.tr: v. 表示；代表
words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.tr: n. 结局；结尾；收场
words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.tr: adj. 破败的；弃置的；
words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.tr: v. 嘲弄；嘲笑
words.ex: They deride him for wearing old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他们嘲笑他穿旧衣服。
words.en: If you deride someone or something, you say that they are stupid or have no value.

words.tr: adj. 嘲笑的；嘲弄的
words.ex: He gave a derisive laugh when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时，他发出了一声嘲笑的笑。
words.en: expressing contempt or ridicule.

words.tr: n. 派生物；衍生物；
words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.tr: v. 得到；源自；来自；
words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.tr: adj. 减损的；毁损的
words.ex: Using derogative language can harm someone's self-esteem.
words.ex_cn: 使用贬低性语言可能会伤害某人的自尊。
words.en: Expressing a low opinion of someone or something; showing a lack of respect.

words.tr: v. 亵渎；污辱；玷污
words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.tr:
adj. 干燥的
v. 使变干；“desiccate”的过去式
words.ex: The desert plants had desiccated leaves.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠植物的叶子已经干枯了。
words.en: Desiccated is used to describe something that has been completely dried out.

words.tr: n. 所愿望之物；迫切需要之物
words.ex: A clean environment is the desideratum for a healthy society.
words.ex_cn: 清洁的环境是健康社会的迫切需要之物。
words.en: Something that is needed or wanted.

words.tr: prep. 尽管；
words.ex: He went to school despite the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去上学了。
words.en: Without being affected by; in spite of.

words.tr: n. 暴君；专制统治者；专制君主
words.ex: The despot ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A despot is a ruler or other person who holds absolute power, typically one who exercises it in a cruel or oppressive way.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: v. 制止；
words.ex: The high fine will deter people from breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款会制止人们违法。
words.en: If something deters you from doing something, it makes you not want to do it or continue doing it.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；
words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr: v. （使）下放；（使） 移交
words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔似的；残忍的；穷凶极恶的
words.ex: The plot of the movie was diabolical, filled with twists and turns.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节充满了曲折和转折，非常恶魔化。
words.en: If you describe something as diabolical, you are emphasizing that it is very bad, extreme, or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 谩骂；抨击
words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.tr: adj. 独裁的；专断的
words.ex: The boss is dictatorial and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 老板很专横，从不听别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as dictatorial, you are criticizing them for behaving in a way that shows they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.tr: v. 区别；区分；辨别；
words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.tr: adj. 无自信的；羞怯的
words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.tr: adj. 残破的；
words.ex: The old house looked dilapidated after years of neglect.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年疏于维护而显得残破。
words.en: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

words.tr: adj. 拖拉的；拖沓的；磨蹭的
words.ex: He gave a dilatory answer to the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师的问题回答得很拖拉。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as dilatory, you mean that they are slow and cause delay.

words.tr: n. 半吊子；浅薄涉猎者；
words.ex: He is a dilettante who likes painting but never practices.
words.ex_cn: 他是个半吊子，喜欢画画但从不练习。
words.en: A dilettante is someone who studies or does something, but is not serious about it and does not have much knowledge.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤奋的
words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.tr:
adj. 极小的；特小的；微小的
n. 小的人；指小词缀；爱称
words.ex: The diminutive cat sat on the small mat.
words.ex_cn: 那只小巧的猫坐在小垫子上。
words.en: A diminutive person or object is very small.

words.tr: v. 消除谬误；使省悟
words.ex: He tried to disabuse her of the idea that money solves everything.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让她明白，钱并不能解决所有问题。
words.en: If you disabuse someone of something, you tell them or persuade them that what they believe is in fact not true.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不忠的；有叛意的
v. 使不满；使疏远；“disaffect”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The disaffected youth joined the protest.
words.ex_cn: 不满的青年加入了抗议活动。
words.en: If you are disaffected, you no longer support or are satisfied with something or someone, especially a group or organization that you used to support.

words.tr: n. 不一致；不和；纷争
words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 分离的；
words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: v. 歧视；
words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不着边际的
words.ex: He gave a discursive speech about many topics.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一篇关于许多主题的散漫演讲。
words.en: If a style of writing or speech is discursive, it includes a lot of information that is not relevant to the main subject.

words.tr: v. 剥夺…的权利（尤指选举权）
words.ex: The law disenfranchises many poor people.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律剥夺了许多穷人的投票权。
words.en: To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to vote or to deprive them of a privilege or a right.

words.tr: adj. 灰心的；气馁的；失望的
words.ex: She felt disheartened after the failure of her project.
words.ex_cn: 项目失败后，她感到很沮丧。
words.en: If you are disheartened, you feel disappointed about something and have less confidence or less hope about it than you did before.

words.tr: adj. 不真诚的；不坦率的；虚伪的
words.ex: He gave a disingenuous answer to avoid trouble.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个不真诚的回答以避免麻烦。
words.en: Someone who is disingenuous is not sincere or honest, but pretends to be so in order to deceive people.

words.tr: adj. 客观的；公正的
words.ex: The judge was disinterested in the case.
words.ex_cn: 法官对这个案件持客观态度。
words.en: If someone is disinterested in something, they have no personal involvement or investment in it and are therefore able to judge it fairly.

words.tr: adj. 完全不同的；
words.ex: The two cultures are disparate in their traditions.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化在传统上完全不同。
words.en: Things that are disparate are clearly different from each other in quality or type.

words.tr: adj. 不动感情的；冷静的；平心静气的
words.ex: She remained dispassionate throughout the heated debate.
words.ex_cn: 她在激烈的辩论中始终保持冷静。
words.en: If you are dispassionate, you are able to act calmly and reasonably and not be influenced by your feelings or by personal opinions.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. （尤指宗教领袖给予的）豁免；特许；分配；制度
words.ex: The priest granted a dispensation from fasting for the sick woman.
words.ex_cn: 神父为这位生病的妇女给予了免于斋戒的豁免。
words.en: A dispensation is a special permission to do something that is not usually allowed, especially in the context of religious or legal systems.

words.tr: v. 掩饰；假装；隐藏
words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 宠爱；娇养；纵容
n. 宠儿
words.ex: She cosseted her baby with soft blankets and gentle songs.
words.ex_cn: 她用柔软的毯子和轻柔的歌声呵护她的婴儿。
words.en: To cosset someone means to treat them with great care and attention, often in a way that is excessive or indulgent.

words.tr: v. 传播；散播；扩散
words.ex: The news will disseminate quickly through social media.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻会通过社交媒体迅速传播。
words.en: To disseminate means to spread or distribute something, especially information, widely.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr: n. 分解；分裂；溶解；解体；解除；死亡
words.ex: The dissolution of sugar in water is quick.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中的分解很快。
words.en: The act or process of ending or breaking up an organization, agreement, or legal arrangement.

words.tr: adj. 温顺的；易驾驭的；
words.ex: The docile dog followed its owner quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这只温顺的狗安静地跟着主人。
words.en: A docile person or animal is quiet, not aggressive, and easily controlled.

words.tr: n. 狗；
words.ex: The dog barks loudly at night.
words.ex_cn: 狗在晚上大声吠叫。
words.en: A dog is a very common four-legged animal that is often kept by people as a pet or to guard or hunt.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；忧愁的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a doleful look after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: A doleful expression, sound, or manner is very sad.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；忧愁的
words.ex: He gave a dolorous look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as dolorous, you mean that it is very sad and depressing.

words.tr: adj. 勇敢强悍的；坚强的；勇猛的; n. (Doughty)人名；(英)道蒂
words.ex: She proved herself a doughty warrior in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 她在逆境中证明了自己是一位勇敢的战士。
words.en: Someone who is doughty is brave and determined.

words.tr: vt. 用鸠尾榫接合；与……吻合; vi. 吻合; n. 楔形榫头
words.ex: The carpenter carefully dovetailed the pieces of wood together.
words.ex_cn: 木匠仔细地将木片用鸠尾榫接合在一起。
words.en: If two things dovetail or if one thing dovetails with another, the two things fit together neatly or have some common characteristics.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr: n. 奸诈；欺骗；口是心非
words.ex: He showed duplicity by lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过对朋友撒谎表现出虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of duplicity, you mean that they are deceitful.

words.tr: n. 胁迫；强迫
words.ex: He signed the paper under duress.
words.ex_cn: 他在胁迫下签了那张纸。
words.en: Duress is a situation in which someone is forced to do something against their will, typically by the use of threats or force.

words.tr: adj. 奔放的；兴高采烈的；沸腾的
words.ex: He is ebullient after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖后非常兴奋。
words.en: If you describe someone as ebullient, you mean that they are lively and full of enthusiasm or excitement about something.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；
words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr: adj. 经济的；节俭的；
words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

words.tr:
adj. 有启发性的
v. 启发；陶冶；启迪；“edify”的现在分词
words.ex: The teacher gave an edifying speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 老师做了一次关于诚实的有启发性的演讲。
words.en: If you describe something as edifying, you mean that it benefits you in some way, especially by teaching you about something.

words.tr: adj. 冒泡的；起泡的；活泼的
words.ex: The champagne was effervescent and bubbled in the glass.
words.ex_cn: 香槟在杯中冒泡沸腾。
words.en: If you describe someone as effervescent, you mean that they are lively, entertaining, enthusiastic, and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 有效的；灵验的
words.ex: This medicine is efficacious for colds.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒有效。
words.en: An efficacious method or treatment is one that has the ability to produce a desired effect or result.

words.tr: n. 厚颜无耻的行为
words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.tr: n. 自大的人；自负的人
words.ex: He is an egotist who only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只谈论自己的自恋者。
words.en: An egotist is someone who is excessively conceited or absorbed in themselves; self-seeker.

words.tr: adj. 极糟的；极坏的
words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.tr: v. 勉强维持；（靠节约）使更持久
words.ex: He had to eke out his income by taking on extra work.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不通过做额外的工作来勉强维持收入。
words.en: To eke means to make a living or support oneself with difficulty, often by adding to what one has in small amounts.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: adj. 挽歌体的；哀悼的；悲伤的
words.ex: The poem has an elegiac tone, reflecting on loss and sorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗有一种挽歌的基调，反映了失落和悲伤。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of an elegy or something that expresses sorrow for something now past.

words.tr: v. 引出；
words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: v. 阐明；
words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.tr: v. 把（某人）难倒；
words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.tr: v. 装饰；
words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；著名的；
words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 移情作用的
words.ex: She is empathetic toward her friend's sadness.
words.ex_cn: 她对朋友的悲伤富有同理心。
words.en: Someone who is empathetic has the ability to share another person's feelings or emotions as if they were their own.

words.tr: n. 经验主义；经验论
words.ex: He believes in empiricism and trusts what he can see.
words.ex_cn: 他相信经验主义，只相信自己能看见的东西。
words.en: The practice of relying on observation and experiment especially in the natural sciences.

words.tr: v. 努力赶上；模仿；
words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.tr: v. 使倾心；使迷恋
words.ex: She was enamored with the beauty of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 她被日落的美景迷住了。
words.en: To fill someone with love or delight; to captivate.

words.tr: adj. 不稳定的；飘忽不定的；
words.ex: The weather has been erratic this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的天气一直不稳定。
words.en: Something that is erratic does not follow a regular pattern, but happens at unexpected times or moves in unexpected directions.

words.tr: adj. 代用的；模仿的
words.ex: The store sells ersatz coffee made from chicory.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售用菊苣制成的代用咖啡。
words.en: An ersatz product is a substitute for another product, especially one that is not as good as the original.

words.tr: adj. 博学的；有学问的
words.ex: The erudite professor knows many ancient languages.
words.ex_cn: 这位博学的教授懂得许多古代语言。
words.en: Having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.tr: v. 避开；回避
words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.tr: adj. 深奥的；
words.ex: The book contains esoteric ideas that only experts understand.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了只有专家才能理解的深奥思想。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest.

words.tr: v. 支持；拥护
words.ex: He espouses simple ideas about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他拥护关于正义的简单理念。
words.en: If you espouse a particular policy, cause, or belief, you become very interested in it and give your support to it.

words.tr: adj. 可估量的；值得尊重的
words.ex: The cost of the project is estimable with current data.
words.ex_cn: 根据当前数据，这个项目的成本是可以估量的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as estimable, you mean that they deserve admiration because they are extremely good or have a very good quality.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.tr: n. 精神欢快；兴高采烈
words.ex: He felt euphoria after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后感到无比兴奋。
words.en: A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

words.tr: adj. 很快消失的；渐消散的；短暂的
words.ex: The evanescent mist disappeared at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 那消散的薄雾在日出时消失了。
words.en: Something that is evanescent quickly disappears or fades away.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.tr: adj. 公平的；公正的；
words.ex: The judge was evenhanded in treating both sides.
words.ex_cn: 法官对双方都公平对待。
words.en: Treating everyone equally and fairly.

words.tr: v. 使加剧；
words.ex: Smoking can exacerbate asthma.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会使哮喘加重。
words.en: If something exacerbates a problem or bad situation, it makes it worse.

words.tr:
adj. 要求严格的；要求小心仔细的；苛求的
v. 强求；急需；要求；“exact”的现在分词
words.ex: He is an exacting teacher who wants perfect work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个要求严格的老师，要求完美无缺的作业。
words.en: requiring a lot of effort, care, or attention

words.tr: v. 赞扬；提升；加强
words.ex: They exalt their hero with cheers.
words.ex_cn: 他们用欢呼赞美他们的英雄。
words.en: To exalt someone or something means to praise them very highly.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使加剧
words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；磨掉（皮）；痛斥
words.ex: The child excoriated his knee when he fell on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子摔倒在粗糙的地面上，膝盖擦伤了。
words.en: To excoriate someone or something means to criticize them severely.

words.tr:
adj. 极痛苦的；极坏的；糟糕透顶的
v. 使痛苦；折磨；施酷刑；“excruciate”的现在分词
words.ex: The pain was excruciating.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛难忍。
words.en: If you describe something as excruciating, you are emphasizing that it is extremely painful, either physically or emotionally.

words.tr: v. 咒骂；痛骂；憎恶
words.ex: He execrates lies and dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他痛恨谎言和不诚实。
words.en: To express great loathing for; to curse or denounce vehemently.

words.tr: n. 解释；注释
words.ex: He wrote an exegesis of the ancient text.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇对古文的阐释。
words.en: Exegesis is the explanation and interpretation of a text, especially a religious one.

words.tr: n. 典型；模范；榜样
words.ex: She was an exemplar of hard work and dedication.
words.ex_cn: 她是勤奋和奉献的典范。
words.en: An exemplar is a person or thing that is considered a very good example of a particular quality or type.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；例证；例示
words.ex: This example exemplifies the rule clearly.
words.ex_cn: 这个例子清楚地说明了这条规则。
words.en: To exemplify means to be a typical example of something or to give an example of something.

words.tr: v. 规劝；告诫
words.ex: The teacher exhorts students to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 老师敦促学生努力学习。
words.en: To strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something.

words.tr: n. 微小；些许，稀少
words.ex: The exiguity of the resources available made the task challenging.
words.ex_cn: 可用资源的微小使得这项任务变得具有挑战性。
words.en: The quality or state of being exiguous; smallness or meagerness.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.tr: adj. 广阔的；
words.ex: The expansive desert stretches for miles.
words.ex_cn: 广阔的沙漠延伸数英里。
words.en: If you describe something such as a period of time or a piece of writing as expansive, you mean that it is very long or detailed.

words.tr: v. 阐述；
words.ex: He expounded his ideas clearly in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上清楚地阐述了他的观点。
words.en: To expound means to explain something in detail, especially a theory, idea, or point of view.

words.tr: v. 清除；抹掉；删除
words.ex: The court decided to expunge his record.
words.ex_cn: 法院决定删除他的记录。
words.en: If you expunge something, you get rid of it completely, because it causes problems or bad feelings.

words.tr: v. 删去（书籍中不合适之处）
words.ex: The teacher expurgated the old book to remove bad words.
words.ex_cn: 老师删改了这本旧书，去掉了不好的词语。
words.en: To remove material that is considered improper or offensive from (a book, movie, etc.).

words.tr: adj. 现存的；
