words.en: If a proposal, principle, or opinion prevails, it gains influence or is accepted, often after a struggle or argument.

words.tr: v. 支吾；搪塞；推诿
words.ex: He prevaricates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他回避回答。
words.en: If you prevaricate, you avoid giving a direct answer or making a firm decision.

words.tr: n. 首位；首要性
words.ex: The primacy of the Pope is a significant aspect of the Catholic Church.
words.ex_cn: 教皇的首位是天主教会的一个重要方面。
words.en: The state of being the most important or first in position or rank.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；崭新的；
words.ex: The forest remained pristine and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林保持原始且未被破坏。
words.en: Something that is pristine is in its original condition and has not been spoiled or damaged.

words.tr: n. 正直；刚直；诚实
words.ex: He is known for his probity in business.
words.ex_cn: 他以商业中的正直著称。
words.en: Probity is the quality of having strong moral principles and honesty.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: adj. 惊人的；巨大的；奇异的；巨大的；
words.ex: He showed a prodigious memory for names.
words.ex_cn: 他对名字有着惊人的记忆力。
words.en: If you describe something as prodigious, you are emphasizing that it is very large or impressive.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.tr: n. 预测；预言；预兆
words.ex: The weatherman's prognostication of rain came true.
words.ex_cn: 气象员的降雨预测成真了。
words.en: A prognostication is a statement about what you think will happen in the future, often based on current signs or evidence.

words.tr: adj. 多产的；
words.ex: He is a prolific writer who publishes books every year.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位多产的作家，每年都会出版书籍。
words.en: A prolific artist, writer, or composer produces a large number of works of art, books, or pieces of music.

words.tr: n. 冗长；罗嗦
words.ex: The judge criticized the lawyer for his prolixity in the court.
words.ex_cn: 法官批评了律师在法庭上的冗长发言。
words.en: Prolixity refers to the use of too many words to express an idea, making speech or writing tediously lengthy.

words.tr: v. 颁布；公布；传播
words.ex: The government will promulgate new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将公布新规则。
words.en: To promulgate means to make a new law or rule known officially and publicly.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr: adj. 有利的；吉祥的；吉利的
words.ex: The weather was propitious for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: If something is propitious, it is likely to lead to success, or it indicates a good chance of success.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: adj. 枯燥的；乏味的；平淡无奇的
words.ex: His prosaic speech bored everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他平淡无奇的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as prosaic, you mean that it is ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: v. 禁止；使失去法律保护
words.ex: The law proscribes selling alcohol to minors.
words.ex_cn: 法律禁止向未成年人出售酒精。
words.en: If a government or other authority proscribes a group or an activity, it officially forbids it or makes it illegal.

words.tr: v. 使改变宗教（或政治）信仰
words.ex: He tries to proselytize his friends about his new religion.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让他的朋友信奉他的新宗教。
words.en: To proselytize means to try to persuade someone to change their religious or political beliefs or way of living to your own.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.tr: adj. 有先见之明的；深谋远虑的
words.ex: He is a provident man who saves money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有远见的人，会为未来存钱。
words.en: Making provision for the future; exercising foresight or forethought.

words.tr: adj. 省的；地方的；
words.ex: The provincial government opened a new school.
words.ex_cn: 省政府开设了一所新学校。
words.en: Relating to a province or provinces; having the manners, viewpoints, etc., considered characteristic of unsophisticated inhabitants of a province; narrow-minded.

words.tr: adj. 临时的；暂时的；
words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.tr: adj. 好战的；好斗的；爱滋事的
words.ex: He is pugnacious and always argues with his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他好斗，总是和同学争吵。
words.en: Someone who is pugnacious is eager to argue or fight.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；强盛的；有势力的
words.ex: The puissant ruler commanded respect from all his subjects.
words.ex_cn: 这位强大的统治者赢得了所有臣民的尊敬。
words.en: Having great power or influence; potent.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.tr: n. 二短音步，抑抑格；（古希腊的）出征舞; adj. 二短音步的，抑抑格的；出征舞的；皮洛士式的，...
words.ex: The victory was a Pyrrhic one, as the cost was too high.
words.ex_cn: 这场胜利是皮洛士式的，因为代价太高了。
words.en: A Pyrrhic victory is a victory that is won but at such a great cost that it is almost a defeat.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.tr: n. 恶心；晕眩；疑虑；不安
words.ex: The smell of the food gave her a qualm.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A qualm is a feeling of uneasiness about whether what you are doing is right.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.tr: adj. 抱怨的；爱发牢骚的
words.ex: She had a querulous tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种爱发牢骚的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as querulous, you mean that they complain about things in a rather bad-tempered way.

words.tr: v. 装备；配备；
words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. 卖国贼
words.ex: He was called a quisling for helping the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为帮助敌人而被称为叛徒。
words.en: A quisling is a person who collaborates with an enemy occupying force, often serving in a puppet government or similar capacity.

words.tr: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；不切实际的
words.ex: He made a quixotic effort to fix the broken bridge with sticks and glue.
words.ex_cn: 他用树枝和胶水试图修复那座破桥，这真是异想天开。
words.en: If you describe someone's ideas or plans as quixotic, you mean that they are imaginative or hopeful but unrealistic.

words.tr: adj. 每日的；平凡的；平常的
words.ex: He drinks coffee every quotidian morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is quotidian occurs every day or is very common and ordinary.

words.tr: n. 善于讲故事的人；健谈者
words.ex: He was known as a raconteur, always able to captivate an audience with his stories.
words.ex_cn: 他以健谈著称，总能用他的故事吸引听众。
words.en: A raconteur is someone who is good at telling stories in an interesting and amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 无赖的；低俗的；放荡不羁的
words.ex: The raffish man stole money from the old woman.
words.ex_cn: 那个无赖的男人从那位老太太那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as raffish, you mean that they are unconventional and attractive in a way that is slightly disreputable.

words.tr: n. 木筏；
words.ex: They crossed the river on a wooden raft.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘着木筏渡过了河。
words.en: A raft is a flat structure made of pieces of wood tied together, which is used as a boat or floating platform.

words.tr: n. 开玩笑
words.ex: He answered with friendly raillery.
words.ex_cn: 他用友好的调侃回应了。
words.en: Raillery is the act of making good-humored jokes or teasing remarks.

words.tr: adj. 放荡的；肆无忌惮的；潇洒的
words.ex: He wore a rakish hat at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上戴了一顶歪斜的帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone as rakish, you mean that they are stylish and confident in a way that is slightly unconventional and possibly a little disreputable.

words.tr: v. 使人耿耿于怀；令人怀恨
words.ex: The unfair comment still rankles him.
words.ex_cn: 那句不公平的话仍让他耿耿于怀。
words.en: If something rankles, it continues to cause you irritation, bitterness, or pain, often because you think it was unfair.

words.tr: n. 友好关系的恢复；和解
words.ex: The two countries began rapprochement after the war.
words.ex_cn: 两国在战争后开始和解。
words.en: An establishment or resumption of harmonious relations between two countries or groups.

words.tr: adj. 高雅的； v. “rarefy”的过去式；
words.ex: He enjoys rarefied art and classical music.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢高雅的艺术和古典音乐。
words.en: Rarefied means made less dense or concentrated, especially in the context of air or gases. It can also refer to something that is elevated in character or nature, often in a way that is considered refined or exclusive.

words.tr: n. 大量同时出现的事件；
words.ex: There was a rash of burglaries last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月发生了一连串的盗窃案。
words.en: If someone is rash or does rash things, they act without thinking carefully first, and therefore make mistakes or behave foolishly.

words.tr: adj. 极饿的；极度的
words.ex: He was ravenous after running five miles.
words.ex_cn: 跑了五英里后，他饿极了。
words.en: If you are ravenous, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr:
v. 指责；斥责
n. 指责；谴责
words.ex: The teacher gave him a rebuke for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而责备了他。
words.en: If you rebuke someone, you speak severely to them because they have said or done something that you do not approve of.

words.tr: n. 概括，重述要点；（生育、生长中对进化等过程的）重演；（尤指奏鸣曲形式中的）再现部
words.ex: The professor's lecture ended with a recapitulation of the main points.
words.ex_cn: 教授的讲座以概括主要观点结束。
words.en: A recapitulation is a summary or brief restatement of the main points of something, especially at the end of a speech, lecture, or piece of writing.

words.tr: v. 调和；
words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.tr: adj. 深奥的；难解的
words.ex: The recondite math problem confused most students.
words.ex_cn: 这道深奥的数学题让大多数学生感到困惑。
words.en: Recondite knowledge or information is known and understood by very few people.

words.tr: n. 反责；揭丑；反控
words.ex: They shouted recrimination at each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们彼此大声指责。
words.en: Recrimination is the act of accusing someone who has accused you of something.

words.tr: v. 复发；再发作
words.ex: The old injury recrudesced after years of inactivity.
words.ex_cn: 多年不活动后，旧伤复发了。
words.en: If something recrudesces, it happens again after it has stopped happening for a while.

words.tr: adj. 可怕的；可敬畏的
words.ex: The redoubtable warrior struck fear into the hearts of his enemies.
words.ex_cn: 那位令人敬畏的战士让敌人心生恐惧。
words.en: If you describe someone as redoubtable, you have great respect for their power and strength, and you may be afraid of them as well.

words.tr: v. 矫正；
words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.tr: v. 驳斥；反驳；批驳；
words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.tr: v. 使降级；转移
words.ex: The team was relegated to the second division after losing all their games.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在输掉所有比赛后被降级到第二级别联赛。
words.en: If you relegate someone or something to a less important position, you give them this position.

words.tr: adj. 相关的；
words.ex: This information is relevant to our project.
words.ex_cn: 这些信息与我们的项目相关。
words.en: Something that is relevant to a situation or person is important or significant in that situation or to that person.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.tr: v. 抗议；表示异议；劝诫
words.ex: He remonstrated with his friend for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为朋友迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To remonstrate means to make a forcefully reproachful protest.

words.tr: v. 背信；食言；否认
words.ex: He reneged on his promise to help me.
words.ex_cn: 他背弃了帮助我的承诺。
words.en: If someone reneges on a promise or an agreement, they do not do what they have promised or agreed to do.

words.tr: adj. 充满的；
words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.tr: n. 堕落的人；不道德的人
words.ex: The townspeople shunned the reprobate, fearing his influence.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的人们都避开那个堕落的人，害怕他的影响。
words.en: A reprobate is a person who behaves in a way that is morally wrong and who shows no regret or shame for their actions.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.tr: v. 废除；撤销
words.ex: The school will rescind the rule next month.
words.ex_cn: 学校下个月将撤销这项规定。
words.en: If a government or a group of people in power rescind a law or agreement, they officially withdraw it and state that it is no longer valid.

words.tr: n. 预定；保留；
words.ex: I made a reservation for two at the restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我在餐厅预订了两个人的座位。
words.en: A reservation is an arrangement whereby something, especially a seat or room, is kept for a particular person who will arrive later.

words.tr: n. 辞职；
words.ex: He handed in his resignation last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周递交了辞职信。
words.en: The act of giving up a job or position in a formal or official way; also refers to the acceptance of something undesirable but inevitable.

words.tr: v. 解决；
words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

words.tr: n. 资源；
words.ex: The school needs more resources for students.
words.ex_cn: 学校需要为学生提供更多的资源。
words.en: A resource is a source or supply from which benefit is produced. Typically resources are materials, energy, services, staff, knowledge, or other assets that are transformed to produce benefit and in the process may be consumed or made unavailable.

words.tr: n. 暂时缓解；
words.ex: The rain gave us a short respite from the heat.
words.ex_cn: 这场雨为我们带来了短暂的凉爽缓解。
words.en: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 不安宁的； 焦躁不安的；难驾驭的；倔强的
words.ex: The audience grew restive as the speaker droned on.
words.ex_cn: 演讲者喋喋不休，听众开始焦躁不安。
words.en: If you are restive, you are impatient or bored with a situation and you want it to change.

words.tr: adj. 复活的；复兴的；恢复活力的
words.ex: The resurgent economy is showing signs of growth.
words.ex_cn: 复苏的经济显示出增长的迹象。
words.en: If something is resurgent, it is becoming more popular or successful again after a period of being less popular or successful.

words.tr: adj. 沉默寡言的；讳莫如深的
words.ex: He is reticent about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的感受很沉默。
words.en: If you are reticent about something, you are unwilling to talk about it or make your feelings known.

words.tr:
adj. 不爱交际的；离群索居的；即将退休的
v. 退休；退役；“retire”的现在分词
words.ex: She was a retiring woman, preferring to spend her evenings at home.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个不爱与人交往的女人，更喜欢在家度过晚上。
words.en: If someone is retiring, they are about to leave their job permanently, usually because of age.

words.tr: v. 撤销；缩回；收回
words.ex: He tried to retract his words after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵后试图收回他的话。
words.en: If you retract something that you have said or written, you say that you did not mean it.

words.tr: adj. 恭敬的；虔诚的
words.ex: He spoke in a reverent tone as he described the ancient temple.
words.ex_cn: 他在描述这座古老寺庙时，语气恭敬。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as reverent, you mean that they are showing great respect for a person or thing.

words.tr: adj. 下流的；粗鄙的
words.ex: His ribald jokes were inappropriate for a family gathering.
words.ex_cn: 他的下流笑话不适合家庭聚会。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as ribald, you mean that it refers to sex in a rude or humorous way.

words.tr: v. 惹恼；激怒
words.ex: His comments about her appearance really riled her.
words.ex_cn: 他对她外貌的评论真的激怒了她。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or irritated.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.tr: n. 排；
words.ex: The students sat in a row.
words.ex_cn: 学生们坐成一排。
words.en: A row is a straight line of things or people. To row means to move a boat through water using oars.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.tr:
adj. 乡村的；纯朴的；土气的
n. 乡下人；乡巴佬
words.ex: They live in a rustic cabin near the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一间乡村小屋里。
words.en: Rustic is used to describe things that are typical of the countryside rather than the town, or things that are simple and old-fashioned in a way that is considered typical of the countryside.

words.tr: adj. 精明练达的；有远见的；有洞察力的
words.ex: He is a sagacious man who always makes wise choices.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个睿智的人，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment; shrewd.

words.tr: adj. 装作圣洁的；伪善的
words.ex: He gave a sanctimonious speech about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一番关于诚实的伪善演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as sanctimonious, you disapprove of them because you think that they are trying to appear morally better than other people.

words.tr:
n. 批准；允许；认可；制裁；处罚
v. 批准；认可；制裁；处罚
words.ex: The company got official sanction to open a new branch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司获得了开设新分公司的正式批准。
words.en: A sanction is a penalty for disobeying a law or rule, or an official permission or approval for an action.

words.tr: n. 镇定；沉着；从容
words.ex: Despite the chaos around him, he maintained his sangfroid.
words.ex_cn: 尽管周围一片混乱，他依然保持冷静。
words.en: If you say that someone has sangfroid, you mean that they are able to remain calm in a dangerous or difficult situation.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.tr: adj. 讥讽的；嘲笑的
words.ex: He gave a sardonic smile when she told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当她说出真相时，他露出了讽刺的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as sardonic, you mean they are mocking or scornful in a humorous way.

words.tr: adj. （男子）服装的；缝纫的
words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.tr: adj. 忧郁的；乖戾的；严肃的
words.ex: He has a saturnine mood and rarely smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他情绪阴郁，很少微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as saturnine, you mean that they are serious and unfriendly.

words.tr: adj. 有见识的；
words.ex: He is savvy about technology.
words.ex_cn: 他对技术很有见识。
words.en: If you describe someone as savvy, you mean that they show a lot of practical knowledge and ability.

words.tr: n. 幸灾乐祸
words.ex: He felt a pang of Schadenfreude when he heard about his rival's failure.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到对手失败的消息时，他感到了一阵幸灾乐祸。
words.en: Schadenfreude is the experience of pleasure, joy, or self-satisfaction that comes from learning of or witnessing the troubles, failures, or humiliation of another.

words.tr: adj. 闪烁的；才气横溢的; v. 闪耀（scintillate 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The sky was filled with scintillating stars.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中满是闪烁的星星。
words.en: If you say that someone is scintillating, you mean that they are lively, intelligent, and amusing.

words.tr: n. 冗长的文章；砂浆层
words.ex: He wrote a long screed about politics.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于政治的长篇大论。
words.en: A long and often tedious speech or piece of writing.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；
words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 自我谦避的；不求闻达的
words.ex: She was self-effacing and never sought the limelight.
words.ex_cn: 她为人谦逊，从不追求聚光灯下的生活。
words.en: Someone who is self-effacing does not like to attract attention to themselves or to their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: n. 外观；样子；相似；表象
words.ex: She tried to maintain a semblance of normality.
words.ex_cn: 她试图维持一种正常的假象。
words.en: The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

words.tr: adj. 说教的；过分认真的；简洁的；富于警句的
words.ex: His speech was full of sententious remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中充满了简洁精炼的格言。
words.en: If you describe someone as sententious, you mean that they try to appear wise, intelligent, and moral, but in a way that is often perceived as pompous or insincere.

words.tr: adj. 感伤的；感情的；多愁善感的
words.ex: He kept the old toy because he was sentimental about it.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了那个旧玩具，因为他对它有感情。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sentimental, you mean that they are influenced by emotional feelings, especially about happy memories of past events or relationships with other people, rather than by careful thought and judgment based on facts.

words.tr: n. 易遇奇缘的运气
words.ex: Finding my lost keys while walking in the park was pure serendipity.
words.ex_cn: 在公园散步时偶然找到了丢失的钥匙，这真是易遇奇缘的运气。
words.en: The occurrence and development of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

words.tr: adj. 平静的；宁静的；安详的
words.ex: The lake is serene in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 清晨的湖面很宁静。
words.en: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled; tranquil.

words.tr: n. 像；幻影；影
words.ex: The statue was a perfect simulacrum of the ancient warrior.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像是古代战士的完美复制品。
words.en: A simulacrum is an image or representation of someone or something, or a superficial likeness or semblance.

words.tr: n. 工作清闲但报酬优厚的职位；闲职；美差
words.ex: He got a sinecure in the government office.
words.ex_cn: 他在政府部门得到了一个闲职。
words.en: A sinecure is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit.

words.tr: adj. 仓促马虎的；毛躁的；潦草的
words.ex: He gave a slapdash answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个草率的回答。
words.en: If you say that something is done in a slapdash way, you mean that it is done carelessly and quickly, without much attention to detail.

words.tr:
n. 浅薄的知识；一知半解；微量
v.  充内行；“smatter”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a smattering of knowledge in many subjects.
words.ex_cn: 他在许多科目上只有一知半解的知识。
words.en: A smattering of something is a small amount of it or a few things about it.

words.tr: adj. 自鸣得意的；沾沾自喜的
words.ex: He smiled in a smug way after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在赢得比赛后得意地笑了。
words.en: If you say that someone is smug, you are criticizing the fact they seem very pleased with how good, clever, or lucky they are.

words.tr:
adj. 讽刺的；刻毒的；卑鄙的
n. 人造宝石；伪币
words.ex: She made a snide comment about his appearance.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的外表进行了暗讽。
words.en: A snide remark or comment is one that criticizes someone in an unkind and indirect way.

words.tr:
v. 冷落；怠慢；不理睬；掐灭
n. 冷落；怠慢
adj. 短平而上翘的
words.ex: He snubbed his friend at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上冷落了朋友。
words.en: To snub someone means to deliberately ignore them or treat them with disrespect, often by refusing to acknowledge their presence or by failing to respond to a greeting or request.

words.tr: n. 违反语法；文法错误；举止失礼
words.ex: He made a solecism when he said 'between you and I'.
words.ex_cn: 当他说出'between you and I'时，犯了一个语法错误。
words.en: A solecism is a grammatical mistake in speech or writing, or a breach of etiquette.

words.tr: adj. 关怀的；切望的；惦记的；悬虑的
words.ex: He was solicitous about her health.
words.ex_cn: 他非常关心她的健康。
words.en: If you are solicitous, you are very concerned about someone's safety, health, or comfort.

words.tr: n. 关怀；牵挂；关切
words.ex: Her eyes showed her deep solicitude for him.
words.ex_cn: 她眼中的深情显示了她对他的深切关怀。
words.en: Solicitude is care or concern for someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 催眠的；让人瞌睡的
n. 安眠药
words.ex: The monotonous lecture was so soporific that I couldn't keep my eyes open.
words.ex_cn: 那个单调乏味的讲座让我昏昏欲睡，眼睛都睁不开了。
words.en: A soporific substance or activity makes you feel sleepy.

words.tr: adj. 卑鄙的；污秽的；肮脏的
words.ex: He made a sordid deal to cheat his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一笔卑鄙的交易来欺骗他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as sordid, you mean that it is very immoral or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 朴素的；清苦的
words.ex: He lives a spartan life with little food and no luxuries.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，食物很少，也没有奢侈品。
words.en: If you describe something as spartan, you mean that it is very simple and not at all luxurious, often because it is intended to be useful or practical rather than attractive.

words.tr: adj. 似是而非的；貌似有理的
words.ex: His argument is specious and misleading.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点看似有理但具有误导性。
words.en: Something that is specious seems to be good, sound, or correct but is actually wrong or false.

words.tr:
adj. 乱花钱的；挥霍的
n. 浪费金钱的人；挥金如土的人
words.ex: He is a spendthrift who buys things he doesn't need.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乱花钱的人，买很多不需要的东西。
words.en: A spendthrift is someone who spends money in an extravagant, irresponsible way.

words.tr: adj. 坏心眼的；脾脏的；容易发怒的; n. 脾气坏的人
words.ex: His splenetic outbursts were becoming increasingly frequent.
words.ex_cn: 他易怒的爆发变得越来越频繁。
words.en: If you describe someone as splenetic, you mean that they easily become very angry about things and express their anger in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

words.tr: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗性的；谬误的
words.ex: The data is spurious and cannot be trusted.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据是虚假的，不可信。
words.en: Something that is spurious seems to be genuine, but is false.

words.tr: v. 轻蔑地拒绝
words.ex: He spurned the offer because it was too low.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个提议，因为报酬太低。
words.en: If you spurn someone or something, you reject them with contempt.

words.tr: v. 浪费；
words.ex: He squandered all his money on games.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都浪费在游戏上了。
words.en: If you squander money, resources, or opportunities, you waste them in a foolish or careless way.

words.tr:
v. 发扑哧声；嘎吱嘎吱的走；压制；遏制
n. 嘎吱声；扑哧声
words.ex: He tried to squelch the rumors about him.
words.ex_cn: 他试图压制关于他的谣言。
words.en: To squelch means to suppress or silence something, often forcefully, or to make a sucking sound as when walking through mud.

words.tr: adj. 古板的；
words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.tr: n. 坚定分子；
words.ex: He is a stalwart of the environmental movement.
words.ex_cn: 他是环保运动的坚定分子。
words.en: A stalwart person is someone who is very loyal and committed to a person, belief, or cause and is not likely to change their views or behavior.

words.tr:
v. 开始；
n. 开始；
words.ex: He starts his day with coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他以喝咖啡开始一天。
words.en: To begin doing something; to cause something to begin or to operate; to set out on a journey.

words.tr:
adj. 忠实的；坚定的
v. 止住（血等的）流出
words.ex: He is a staunch supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的坚定支持者。
words.en: A staunch person is someone who is very loyal and firm in their beliefs or support for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 坚定的；不动摇的
words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.tr: n. 薪金；助学金
words.ex: He receives a small stipend for his internship.
words.ex_cn: 他因实习获得少量薪金。
words.en: A stipend is a sum of money paid regularly as a salary or allowance.

words.tr: adj. 不动声色的；无动于衷的；不易激动的
words.ex: He remained stolid in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 面对逆境，他依然冷漠。
words.en: If you describe someone as stolid, you mean that they do not show much emotion or are not very exciting or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 严苛的；
words.ex: The school has stringent rules about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学校对作业有严格的规定。
words.en: Stringent measures, rules, or conditions are very strict or severe.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.tr: v. 阻碍；阻挠；
words.ex: The rain stymied our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨水阻碍了我们去远足的计划。
words.en: To stymie someone or something means to prevent them from achieving their aims.

words.tr: v. 归入；包含；包括
words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.tr: n. 遁词；诡计；托辞；
words.ex: He used subterfuge to avoid answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 他用遁词来避免回答问题。
words.en: Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal.

words.tr:
adj. 颠覆性的；破坏性的
n. 颠覆分子；危险分子
words.ex: The subversive poster tried to break the government's rules.
words.ex_cn: 那张颠覆性的海报试图破坏政府的规则。
words.en: A subversive person or activity is one that is intended to weaken or destroy a political system or government.

words.tr: adj. 面有愠色的；闷闷不乐的；阴沉的
words.ex: He gave a sullen look when his mom asked him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他一脸阴沉。
words.en: Someone who is sullen is bad-tempered and does not speak much.

words.tr: n. 顶峰；首脑会议；
words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；目空一切的；自大的
words.ex: He gave a supercilious smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is supercilious, you disapprove of them because they behave in a way that shows they think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.tr: v. 取代；排挤掉；
words.ex: Smartphones supplanted landline phones.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机取代了固定电话。
words.en: To supplant someone or something means to take the place of them, often by being more powerful or effective.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；乖戾的；傲慢的
words.ex: The surly man refused to say hello.
words.ex_cn: 那个脾气暴躁的人拒绝打招呼。
words.en: If someone is surly, they are unfriendly and bad-tempered.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；鬼鬼祟祟的；偷偷摸摸的
words.ex: He gave a surreptitious glance at his phone during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时偷偷瞥了一眼手机。
words.en: If something is done surreptitiously, it is done secretly, often because it would not be approved of.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.tr: n. 长篇抨击激烈演说
words.ex: He went on a tirade about slow internet.
words.ex_cn: 他大发雷霆，抱怨网速太慢。
words.en: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

words.tr: n. 麻木；迟钝；萎靡
words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.tr: adj. 弯曲的；
words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.tr: adj. 短暂的
words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；
words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.tr: v. 使变化；使转化
words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.tr:
n. 艰辛；艰苦劳动；痛苦；分娩的阵痛
v. 辛苦工作；发生或经受阵痛
words.ex: His travail helped him succeed in the end.
words.ex_cn: 他的艰辛最终让他取得了成功。
words.en: Travail refers to painful or laborious effort, especially in the context of work or childbirth.

words.tr:
n. 滑稽拙劣的模仿；嘲弄；歪曲
v. 滑稽化；嘲弄
words.ex: The trial was a travesty of justice.
words.ex_cn: 这场审判是对正义的嘲弄。
words.en: If you describe something as a travesty of another thing, you mean that it is a very bad representation of that other thing.

words.tr: adj. 危险的；
words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.tr: n. 苦难；磨难；痛苦
words.ex: The tribulations of war left many families devastated.
words.ex_cn: 战争的苦难使许多家庭陷入了绝望。
words.en: A tribulation is a cause of great trouble or suffering.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；
words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.tr: n. 凶猛；粗暴；好斗
words.ex: The truculence of the opponent's team was evident in their aggressive play.
words.ex_cn: 对手球队的好战性在他们激烈的比赛中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being eager or quick to argue, fight, or start a conflict; aggressiveness.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.tr: v. 截短；修剪；修短
words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.tr: n. 骚动；骚乱；心烦意乱
words.ex: The crowd caused a tumult after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，人群引起了混乱。
words.en: A tumult is a state of confusion, noise, and excitement, often involving a large group of people.

words.tr: adj. 浮肿的；肿胀的；浮夸的
words.ex: His legs looked turgid after the long walk.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间走路后，双腿看起来浮肿了。
words.en: If you describe something such as a piece of writing or a speech as turgid, you think it is boring and difficult to understand because it is too serious or complicated.

words.tr: n. 堕落；卑鄙；邪恶
words.ex: His actions were marked by turpitude and deceit.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为充满了卑鄙和欺骗。
words.en: Turpitude refers to depravity or wickedness, especially in a moral sense.

words.tr: n. 初学者；生手；新手
words.ex: As a tyro in the field, he found the learning curve quite steep.
words.ex_cn: 作为这个领域的新手，他发现学习曲线相当陡峭。
words.en: A tyro is someone who is new to and therefore inexperienced at a particular activity.

words.tr: n. 树荫；不快；怨恨
words.ex: We sat under the umbrage of the big tree.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在大树的树荫下。
words.en: A feeling of pique or resentment at some often fancied slight or insult.

words.tr: adj. 无可争辩的；攻不破的；不容置疑的
words.ex: His alibi is unassailable.
words.ex_cn: 他的不在场证明是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something such as a person's reputation or an argument as unassailable, you mean that it cannot be criticized or attacked because it is completely right or true.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.tr: adj. 不让步的；不妥协的；强硬的
words.ex: He is uncompromising about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他在诚实方面毫不妥协。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncompromising, you mean that they are determined not to change their opinions or aims in any way.

words.tr: adj. 违背良心的；无节制的；过度的
words.ex: The prices they were charging were unconscionable.
words.ex_cn: 他们收取的价格是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unconscionable, you mean that it is morally unacceptable, often because it is too large, too extreme, or too severe.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr: v. 强调；
words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: v. 承担经济责任；承保；承销
words.ex: The bank will underwrite the new project.
words.ex_cn: 银行将为这个新项目提供担保。
words.en: To agree to pay for a possible loss or damage, especially in insurance; to agree to buy all the shares that are not bought by the public in a new company, or to arrange for this to be done.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.tr: adj. 镇定自若的；临危不乱的
words.ex: She remained unflappable even under intense pressure.
words.ex_cn: 即使在巨大的压力下，她依然保持镇定。
words.en: If you describe someone as unflappable, you mean that they stay calm in difficult or worrying situations.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.tr: v. 使失去勇气；使身心交疲；使气馁
words.ex: The loud noise unnerves her.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她心神不宁。
words.en: If something unnerves you, it makes you feel worried or uncomfortable.

words.tr: adj. 前所未有的；
words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr: adj. 不讨人喜欢的；不吸引人的；
words.ex: He has an unprepossessing appearance, but he is very kind.
words.ex_cn: 他外表不讨人喜欢，但他非常善良。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unprepossessing, you mean that they look rather plain or ordinary, and not at all impressive or attractive.

words.tr: adj. 不吉利的；不顺遂的
words.ex: The weather was unpropitious for the outdoor event.
words.ex_cn: 天气对户外活动不利。
words.en: If you describe something as unpropitious, you mean that it is likely to lead to failure or be unfavorable.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 不道德的；
words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.tr: adj. 不体面的；不相配的；不适宜的
words.ex: It is unseemly to shout in a library.
words.ex_cn: 在图书馆大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that someone's behaviour is unseemly, you disapprove of it because it is not appropriate in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 大量地给予的；不吝啬的
words.ex: She was unstinting in her praise for the volunteers.
words.ex_cn: 她对志愿者们给予了慷慨的赞扬。
words.en: If you describe someone's support or effort as unstinting, you mean that they give it generously and completely, without holding back.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；麻烦的；异常的；意外的；棘手的
words.ex: He faced untoward remarks from his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他遭到了同学的不友好的评论。
words.en: If you say that something is untoward, you mean that it is unexpected and causes difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 自由的；不受约束的
words.ex: She felt an untrammeled sense of freedom while hiking in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中徒步时感受到了一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: Not limited or restricted; free.

words.tr: v. 斥责；责骂
words.ex: She upbraided him for his carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 她因他的粗心大意而责骂他。
words.en: To criticize or reproach severely; to scold.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.tr: v. 征服；克服；击败
words.ex: The hero will vanquish the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 英雄将战胜龙。
words.en: To vanquish someone means to defeat them completely in a battle or a competition.

words.tr: n. 差额；
words.ex: There is a large variance between the budget and the actual cost.
words.ex_cn: 预算与实际成本之间有很大的差额。
words.en: Variance refers to the fact or quality of being different, divergent, or inconsistent.

words.tr: adj. 吹嘘的
words.ex: The vaunted new technology turned out to be a disappointment.
words.ex_cn: 这项被大肆吹嘘的新技术结果令人失望。
words.en: If you describe something as vaunted or much vaunted, you mean that people praise it more than it deserves.

words.tr: adj. （感情）强烈的；激烈的
words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.tr: n. 受贿
words.ex: The venality of the officials led to widespread corruption.
words.ex_cn: 官员的唯利是图导致了普遍的腐败。
words.en: The quality or state of being venal; readiness to sell one's services or influence for money or other benefits.

words.tr: n. 表层饰板；
words.ex: The table has a wooden veneer on top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的表面有一层木制饰板。
words.en: A veneer is a thin layer of wood or other material that is used to cover a surface, especially in furniture making, to make it look more attractive.

words.tr: v. 崇敬；
words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.tr: adj. 轻微的；可原谅的
words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.tr: n. 貌似真实；逼真
words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

words.tr: adj. 间接体验的；
words.ex: He enjoyed the adventure through vicarious experiences in books.
words.ex_cn: 他通过书中的间接体验享受了冒险。
words.en: Experienced or felt by watching, hearing about, or reading about someone else rather than by doing something yourself.

words.tr: n. 变迁兴衰
words.ex: Life is full of vicissitude.
words.ex_cn: 生活充满起伏。
words.en: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 竞争；争夺
words.ex: They vie for the top prize.
words.ex_cn: 他们争夺最高奖项。
words.en: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.

words.tr: v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.tr: v. 为…辩护；证明…正当
words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.tr: adj. 想复仇的；报复性的；怀恨的
words.ex: He was vindictive and refused to forgive her.
words.ex_cn: 他心怀报复，拒绝原谅她。
words.en: If you say that someone is vindictive, you are critical of them because they deliberately try to upset or cause trouble for someone who they think has done them harm.

words.tr: n. 泼妇；悍妇
words.ex: The virago shouted loudly at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 那个泼妇对司机大喊大叫。
words.en: A virago is a woman who is very aggressive or domineering.

words.tr: n. 硫酸，[无化] 硫酸盐；尖刻的话; vt. 用硫酸处理；用尖刻的话伤害
words.ex: His vitriol comments left her feeling hurt and defensive.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的评论让她感到受伤和防备。
words.en: Vitriol is a term used to describe cruel and bitter criticism or comments.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；恶意的
words.ex: His vitriolic words hurt everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他刻薄的话伤害了房间里所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as vitriolic, you disapprove of it because it is full of bitterness and hate, and so causes a lot of distress and pain.

words.tr: v. 辱骂；谩骂；痛斥
words.ex: He vituperates his boss for unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因为不公平的待遇而痛骂他的老板。
words.en: To criticize or blame someone harshly and angrily.

words.tr: adj. 大声喊叫的；喧嚷的
words.ex: The vociferous crowd shouted for change.
words.ex_cn: 喧闹的人群大声要求变革。
words.en: If you describe someone as vociferous, you mean that they speak with great energy and determination, because they want their views to be heard.

words.tr: n. 流利；健谈
words.ex: Her volubility made it hard for anyone else to get a word in.
words.ex_cn: 她的健谈使得其他人很难插上话。
words.en: The quality of talking fluently, readily, or incessantly.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

words.tr: v. 想要；“want”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is wanting a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一辆新自行车。
words.en: If something is wanting, it is lacking or not good enough in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 恣意的；不负责的
words.ex: The wanton destruction of the forest shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 对森林的恣意破坏让每个人都感到震惊。
words.en: If someone describes a person or their behaviour as wanton, they are critical of them for behaving in a very uncontrolled or unacceptable way, often without caring about the consequences.

words.tr:
n. 蜡；
v. 给…上蜡；
words.ex: Bees make wax to build their hives.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂用蜡建造蜂巢。
words.en: Wax is a solid, slightly shiny substance made of fat or oil that is used to make candles, polish, and other products. It can also refer to the process of applying wax to something or the natural substance found in the ear.

words.tr: adj. 异想天开的；古怪的；反复无常的
words.ex: The little girl wore a whimsical hat with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩戴着一顶带有花朵的古怪帽子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as whimsical, you mean that they are unusual, playful, and unpredictable, often in a way that you find charming or amusing.

words.tr: adj. 漂亮的；迷人的；讨人喜欢的
words.ex: The winsome girl smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个可爱的女孩对每个人微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as winsome, you mean that they are attractive and charming.

words.tr: n. 时代精神；时代思潮
words.ex: The film captures the zeitgeist of the 1960s.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影捕捉到了20世纪60年代的时代精神。
words.en: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history as shown by the ideas and beliefs of the time.

words.tr: n. 顶点；天顶；全盛
words.ex: The sun is at its zenith at noon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在正午时分达到最高点。
words.en: The zenith is the time at which something is most powerful or successful.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生（或出版等）的；准备好的；
words.ex: The forthcoming book will be released next month.
words.ex_cn: 即将出版的这本书将在下个月发布。
words.en: If something is forthcoming, it is happening or coming soon.

words.tr: adj. 可行的；
words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.
